Content: Source: Paul Deane, junior officer, “The Tragedy of the Survivors,” The Nation, `text(October 1930)`.

`text(One)` was not always attacking or under fire. And `text(one’s)` friends were not always being killed. `text(One)` had friends in those `text(days)`, and `text(one)` has hardly any now. And friendship was good in brief rests in some French village behind the line where it was sometimes spring and there were still fruit trees in bloom, and young cornfields, and birds singing. And even after the `text(first)` great disillusionment, that followed the Somme,* reached England through men coming home, young officers still went out from school full of enthusiasm. `text(One)` wanted to go there oneself and see what it was like, even though `text(one)` knew.
